coverage_notes:
CHAMPIONSHIP VERIFIED: Indiana finished 16-0 (9-0 Big Ten) and beat Miami (FL) 27-21 in the CFP National Championship Game on January 19, 2026 — the first national title in program history. Confirmed on the Wikipedia team-season page.

PRIMARY SOURCE: The best source by far was Indiana's own official page at iuhoosiers.com/sports/football/coaches, headed "2025 Football Staff", captured by the Wayback Machine on 2026-01-13 (timestamp 20260113182706) — six days before the championship game. That capture is essentially a championship-eve snapshot and lists 47 people in two tables: "Coaching Staff" (12) and "Support Staff" (35). All 47 rows are reported here. The Wikipedia team-season page corroborates the 12 coaching-staff members but lists no support staff, so it is attached as a second source only for those 12.

QUOTE METHODOLOGY (important for mechanical matching): on the IU page, each person's name and title live in SEPARATE <td> cells with no whitespace text node between them, so a combined "Name Title" string does not exist anywhere in the page source and would fail a substring match. Every quote I supply is therefore a single contiguous cell value. Each person gets two source entries from the same URL: one quoting the Name cell, one quoting the Title cell, with notes tying them to the same table row. I verified programmatically that all 94 IU quotes appear as exact substrings under four different HTML-to-text conventions (tags stripped to empty, tags stripped to space, and both with whitespace collapsed). The 12 Wikipedia quotes are contiguous in the source ("Bryant Haines (Defensive coordinator/linebackers)") and match under three of those four conventions; they fail only under the unusual tags-to-space-without-collapsing convention.

TWO NAME QUIRKS: the IU page renders "Michael  Turner, MS, LAT, ATC" and "Nick  Pappas" with a DOUBLE internal space. Rather than risk a whitespace-normalization mismatch, I quoted the unambiguous sub-strings "Turner, MS, LAT, ATC" and "Pappas" (each occurs exactly once on the page). Names in the name field are cleaned of credential suffixes (e.g. "Kyle Blackman" rather than "Kyle Blackman, MS, LAT, ATC"); the full credentialed string is what appears in the quote.

MID-SEASON CHANGES (ring rule = on staff at the championship game): I diffed the Jan 13, 2026 capture against the Aug 28, 2025 capture (two days before the season opener) and the Jul 9, 2025 capture. Two people arrived after the season started and are flagged with midseason_note: Michael Conway and Sales Pinckney. THREE PEOPLE ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED because they were gone by the championship-eve capture: Gage Proctor (Assistant Director of Player Personnel — present Aug 28, 2025, absent Jan 13, 2026, so he departed during the season); Tee McCann (Assistant Director of Graphic Design) and Whitney Dean (Equipment Manager, Football), both present Jul 9, 2025 but already gone by Aug 28, 2025, i.e. preseason departures. One title changed during the year: Darrell Grant went from "Director of Creative Video" to "Director of Football Creative Video"; the championship-eve wording is used.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT: (1) No graduate assistants appear anywhere in the official directory — the gradasst category is empty, and I did not pad it. Indiana's public staff page may simply not list GAs, so I cannot say whether the team had any. (2) The directory almost certainly omits student assistants, interns, and recruiting/creative student workers. (3) I could not locate a 2025 media guide on the school site, archive.org, or issuu to cross-check for additional names. (4) A Wayback capture from 2025-12-12 exists but archive.org rate-limiting (repeated 429/503) defeated six retry attempts; it would have narrowed the arrival windows for Conway and Pinckney, though it would not change the championship-eve roster. (5) This session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before I started, so I could not consult contemporary news hire announcements or championship coverage — every row here rests on the official athletics directory plus Wikipedia, with no news corroboration. (6) Role categories are my mapping of IU's wording; two are judgment calls worth noting: Josh Huff ("Sports Science Coordinator") is filed under sc alongside the athletic-performance staff, and Isaac Hicks III ("Director of Sports Performance Nutrition") is filed under medical. Jared Coulter ("Team Analyst/Football Video Coordinator") is filed under analyst though the role is partly video operations.
